rationale: Sourced the leader-side consequence that the account had left as an inference, by reading what the leader does with the success the damaged follower returns. A successful AppendEntries response advances that peer's nextIndex past the accepted entry and records the peer's match index in the leader's commitment, and the commitment set contains voters only, so the accepted entry is both counted as replicated for that peer and never revisited; the leader has no reason to send the shapes that would read across the gap. I recorded that as a behavior entry with two new anchors, which narrows what remains unmeasured in the store-failure account from 'what the leader does with the acknowledgement' to the live-leader sequence itself.

knowledge.statement: A successful AppendEntries response moves the leader's bookkeeping forward for that peer and counts it where voters are counted. On success the replication loop takes the last entry of the request, sets the peer's nextIndex to one past it and calls the commitment's match for that peer, and the commitment's match index map is built only from servers whose suffrage is Voter, both when it is created and when a new configuration is set on it. A follower that answered success for an entry is therefore recorded as matching it, is never sent that range again, and - when it is a voter - its acknowledgement counts toward the leader's quorum for committing that entry.
knowledge.conditions: Leader replicating to a configured peer whose response carried Success true, with a log store on the leader that still holds the entries being replicated; the counting only includes peers that appear in the leader's latest configuration as voters.
